exposure: perineal body biometrics (area, anteroposterior diameter, lateral diameter)
cohort: Pregnant women at 36-40 weeks of gestation.
finding: Specific perineal and anal sphincter biometric measurements (e.g., larger perineal body area, thicker EAS, smaller anteroposterior/lateral diameters, thinner IAS) and higher elastic modulus in the ninth month of pregnancy were associated with an increased risk of perineal tears.
cross-section timing: 36-40 weeks of gestation (ninth month of pregnancy)
